questions.stem: Which process removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere?

options.text: Respiration
Combustion
Photosynthesis
Decomposition

questions.explanation: Green plants fix carbon dioxide into carbohydrate during photosynthesis, which is the main natural route by which carbon leaves the air. Respiration, combustion and decomposition all oxidise carbon compounds and return carbon dioxide to the atmosphere.

distractorRationale.b: Combustion of wood and fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide
distractorRationale.d: Decomposers respire and release carbon dioxide from dead matter

questions.stem: Rhizobium bacteria in the root nodules of cowpea are important because they

options.text: convert nitrate to nitrogen gas
fix atmospheric nitrogen into compounds the plant can use
convert ammonia to nitrite
cause eutrophication

questions.explanation: Rhizobium is a nitrogen-fixing symbiont: it turns unreactive N₂ into ammonium compounds that the cowpea uses to make protein, and the plant feeds the bacterium. That is why legumes restore soil fertility in crop rotation.

distractorRationale.a: Denitrifying bacteria such as Pseudomonas convert nitrate to nitrogen gas
distractorRationale.c: Nitrosomonas converts ammonia to nitrite during nitrification
distractorRationale.d: Eutrophication is caused by excess nitrate and phosphate in water, not by Rhizobium

questions.stem: Carbon monoxide is a dangerous air pollutant because it

options.text: causes acid rain by dissolving in rainwater
combines more readily with haemoglobin than oxygen does
destroys the ozone layer
is the main gas responsible for eutrophication

questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide from incomplete combustion binds to haemoglobin to form carboxyhaemoglobin, so the blood carries far less oxygen and tissues suffocate. Acid rain is caused by sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides, not by carbon monoxide.

distractorRationale.a: Sulphur dioxide, not carbon monoxide, is the usual cause of acid rain
distractorRationale.c: Ozone depletion is linked to chlorofluorocarbons, not carbon monoxide
distractorRationale.d: Eutrophication is caused by mineral nutrients in water, not by a gas in air

questions.stem: The correct sequence in nitrification is

options.text: nitrate → nitrite → ammonia
ammonia → nitrite → nitrate
nitrogen gas → protein → nitrate
nitrate → nitrogen gas → ammonia

questions.explanation: After ammonification, Nitrosomonas oxidises ammonia to nitrite and Nitrobacter oxidises nitrite to nitrate, the form most plants absorb. The reverse sequence is not nitrification; conversion of nitrate to nitrogen gas is denitrification.

distractorRationale.a: This is the reverse of nitrification
distractorRationale.c: This mixes fixation, protein synthesis and uptake, and skips the named nitrifying steps
distractorRationale.d: Nitrate to nitrogen gas is denitrification

questions.stem: Eutrophication of a fish pond after heavy fertiliser use on nearby farms is caused by

options.text: oil coating the surface and blocking light
nitrate and phosphate runoff that triggers an algal bloom, then oxygen depletion when the algae die and decay
carbon monoxide dissolving in the water
plastic bags reducing the volume of the pond

questions.explanation: Nitrates and phosphates from fertiliser are plant nutrients. They cause algae to multiply; when the bloom dies, decomposers use up dissolved oxygen and fish suffocate. Oil spills and plastics pollute water in other ways but are not eutrophication.

distractorRationale.a: Oil spills smother organisms but that is not the definition of eutrophication
distractorRationale.c: Carbon monoxide is an air pollutant that binds haemoglobin
distractorRationale.d: Plastic is a physical pollutant, not a nutrient that fertilises algae

questions.stem: Which of the following is a method of conserving natural resources in Nigeria?

options.text: Uncontrolled bush burning every dry season
Establishing national parks such as Yankari and Cross River
Dumping untreated sewage into rivers
Clear-felling mangrove for charcoal with no replanting

questions.explanation: National parks legally protect habitats and wildlife so that species and ecosystems can persist. Yankari (Bauchi) and Cross River National Park are named Nigerian examples that WAEC accepts. The other options destroy resources rather than conserve them.

distractorRationale.a: Bush burning destroys vegetation, soil organisms and stored carbon
distractorRationale.c: Sewage dumping pollutes water and spreads disease
distractorRationale.d: Clear-felling mangrove without replacement removes a protective coastal ecosystem

questions.stem: Waterlogged soil on a rice plot loses nitrate even though no crop has been harvested. The most likely explanation is

options.text: Nitrosomonas converting nitrate to ammonia
denitrifying bacteria converting nitrate to nitrogen gas
Rhizobium absorbing all the nitrate
photosynthesis using up the nitrate

questions.explanation: Low oxygen in waterlogged soil favours denitrifying bacteria such as Pseudomonas, which use nitrate as an electron acceptor and release N₂. That is why badly drained fields lose fertility even without leaching or harvest. Rhizobium fixes nitrogen; it does not strip nitrate in this way, and photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide, not nitrate as a carbon source.

distractorRationale.a: Nitrosomonas oxidises ammonia to nitrite; it does not reverse nitrification
distractorRationale.c: Rhizobium fixes N₂; rice is not a legume hosting Rhizobium nodules
distractorRationale.d: Photosynthesis does not consume soil nitrate as its carbon source

questions.stem: A crude-oil spill in a Niger Delta mangrove creek is followed by dead fish and blackened roots. Which conservation response addresses both the pollution and the long-term carbon cycle?

options.text: Leave the oil in place so it can fertilise the mangrove
Clean the spill, enforce pipeline laws, and restore mangrove by planting, because mangrove stores carbon and shelters fisheries
Add more nitrogen fertiliser to speed eutrophication and hide the oil
Burn the remaining mangrove to release the trapped oil as carbon monoxide

questions.explanation: Oil is toxic, not a fertiliser; cleaning, legal control of spills and replanting restore the habitat. Healthy mangrove sequesters carbon, protects the shoreline and supports fish nurseries, so restoration serves conservation and the carbon cycle together. Fertiliser and burning would worsen pollution.

distractorRationale.a: Crude oil coats roots and gills; it does not fertilise mangrove
distractorRationale.c: Eutrophication strips oxygen and would kill still more fish
distractorRationale.d: Burning remaining trees adds air pollution and destroys the carbon store
